## How they got there
Inter reached the final as runners-up after losing to Manchester City 0-1. Their profile was defined by elite efficiency, boasting a shot accuracy of 59.3% that placed them better than 97% of their season's group-phase peers and a shot conversion rate of 18.5% superior to 62% of those same teams. They also relied on a direct approach with long passes accounting for 12.9% of their total volume, a metric higher than 62% of the league phase squads they faced.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would not have selected Inter as a finalist contender, ranking them 14th out of 16 knockout teams with only a 2.9% probability of reaching the final compared to a base rate of 12.5%. This low confidence aligns with an expected performance level nearest to "out before quarter-finals," indicating the model viewed their path as significantly more difficult than reality suggested.

## Weak spots
The team displayed clear vulnerabilities in defensive metrics, allowing opponent shots on target per game at a value of 5.7 which was better than only 23% of that season's group-phase teams. They also conceded an average of 10.7 opponent shots per game and generated just 9.0 shots per game themselves, ranking in the bottom half of their league phase peers for both categories. These statistical associations suggest a profile where defensive solidity and shot volume were less dominant than their finishing efficiency implied.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
